quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'only' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Only she knew the real reason behind the decision.
quests.hint: 'Only' before the subject restricts who knew - no one else.
quests.explanation: 'Only' before 'she': 'Only she knew'. This means no one but her knew. Compare 'She only knew' (she knew but didn't act) - different meaning.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'only' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She only knows the basics of the system.
quests.hint: 'Only' before the verb limits what she does - she knows but nothing more.
quests.explanation: 'Only' before 'knows': 'only knows the basics'. This limits the extent of her knowledge. Contrast with 'Only she knows' (she is the only person who knows).

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'only' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She knows only the basics of the system.
quests.hint: 'Only' directly before the object limits what is known.
quests.explanation: 'Only' before 'the basics': 'knows only the basics'. This limits the content of her knowledge. The position of 'only' shifts the focus.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'even' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Even he admitted the plan had serious flaws.
quests.hint: 'Even' before the subject signals surprise that this person would admit it.
quests.explanation: 'Even' before 'he': 'Even he admitted'. It implies he was the least likely person to admit the flaws.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'even' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: He even admitted the plan had serious flaws.
quests.hint: 'Even' before the verb signals that admitting was an unexpected action for him.
quests.explanation: 'Even' before 'admitted': 'he even admitted'. It emphasises that admission was the surprising action - he went so far as to admit it.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'even' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: He admitted the plan had even more serious flaws.
quests.hint: 'Even' before a comparative signals the degree exceeds expectations.
quests.explanation: 'Even' before 'more serious': 'even more serious flaws'. It intensifies the comparison, showing the flaws were more serious than expected.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'simply' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She simply does not understand the problem.
quests.hint: 'Simply' before 'does not' reinforces the negation.
quests.explanation: 'Simply' before 'does not': 'simply does not understand'. It emphasises the completeness of her failure to understand.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'merely' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: He merely glanced at the document before signing it.
quests.hint: 'Merely' before the verb minimises the action taken.
quests.explanation: 'Merely' before 'glanced': 'merely glanced'. It minimises the action - he did no more than a quick look.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'just' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She just passed the exam by one mark.
quests.hint: 'Just' before a verb meaning 'only barely' shows narrow success.
quests.explanation: 'Just' before 'passed': 'just passed'. It signals she barely succeeded, with very little margin.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'almost' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: He almost never takes a day off work.
quests.hint: 'Almost' before a frequency adverb modifies the frequency itself.
quests.explanation: 'Almost' before 'never': 'almost never'. It means he very rarely takes a day off - close to never but not quite.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'nearly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She is nearly always late for morning meetings.
quests.hint: 'Nearly' before 'always' modifies the frequency adverb.
quests.explanation: 'Nearly' before 'always': 'nearly always late'. It means she is late very frequently - close to always but not quite.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'hardly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: He can hardly ever find time to read for pleasure.
quests.hint: 'Hardly' before 'ever' creates a strong near-negative frequency.
quests.explanation: 'Hardly' before 'ever': 'hardly ever find time'. It means he very rarely - almost never - finds time to read.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'alone' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She alone knew where the documents were hidden.
quests.hint: 'Alone' after the subject means 'only she - no one else'.
quests.explanation: 'Alone' immediately after 'she': 'She alone knew'. This structure emphasises exclusive knowledge - only she knew.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'themselves' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: They built the entire house themselves.
quests.hint: Reflexive intensifiers come at the END of the sentence or directly after the object.
quests.explanation: 'Themselves' comes at the end: 'built the entire house themselves'. The reflexive intensifier emphasises they did it without help.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'himself' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The president himself signed the declaration.
quests.hint: Intensifying reflexives come directly after the noun they emphasise.
quests.explanation: 'Himself' comes directly after 'president': 'The president himself'. The intensifier immediately follows the noun to show personal involvement.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'well' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The speech went down well with the entire audience.
quests.hint: 'Well' as an adverb of manner follows the verb phrase.
quests.explanation: 'Well' follows 'went down': 'went down well'. It describes how the speech was received by the audience.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'abroad' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She had studied abroad for two years before returning.
quests.hint: Adverbs of place follow the verb they modify.
quests.explanation: 'Abroad' follows 'studied': 'studied abroad'. Place adverbs follow the verb.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'apart' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: They live a thousand miles apart and only meet in summer.
quests.hint: 'Apart' follows the noun phrase or description it modifies.
quests.explanation: 'Apart' follows 'a thousand miles': 'a thousand miles apart'. This adverb expresses separation distance after the measurement.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'personally' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: I personally think the second design is far superior.
quests.hint: 'Personally' as a stance adverb can come between the subject and verb for emphasis.
quests.explanation: 'Personally' between 'I' and 'think': 'I personally think'. It emphasises this is the speaker's individual view.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'sincerely' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: I sincerely hope this matter can be resolved quickly.
quests.hint: Manner adverbs go between the subject and modal/main verb.
quests.explanation: 'Sincerely' between 'I' and 'hope': 'I sincerely hope'. It intensifies the genuine nature of the hope.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'deeply' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: I deeply regret the inconvenience this has caused you.
quests.hint: Degree adverbs go before the verb they intensify.
quests.explanation: 'Deeply' before 'regret': 'I deeply regret'. It intensifies the sincerity and strength of the regret.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'long' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She had long dreamed of starting her own business.
quests.hint: 'Long' meaning 'for a long time' goes between 'had' and the past participle.
quests.explanation: 'Long' between 'had' and 'dreamed': 'had long dreamed'. It indicates the dream existed over an extended period.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'well' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She was well aware of the risks involved in the project.
quests.hint: 'Well' as a degree adverb can intensify adjectives, coming before them.
quests.explanation: 'Well' before 'aware': 'well aware'. It intensifies 'aware', meaning she was thoroughly and fully aware.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'much' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She was much relieved to hear the positive news.
quests.hint: 'Much' as a degree adverb intensifies past participle adjectives.
quests.explanation: 'Much' before 'relieved': 'much relieved'. 'Much' intensifies the participle adjective, meaning very relieved.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'better' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The new system works far better than the old one.
quests.hint: 'Far' intensifies 'better' - but 'better' itself must come after 'works far'.
quests.explanation: 'Better' comes after 'far': 'works far better'. The adverb 'better' comes after the verb phrase it modifies.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'readily' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She readily agreed to take on the additional responsibility.
quests.hint: Manner adverbs often come before the main verb.
quests.explanation: 'Readily' before 'agreed': 'readily agreed'. It means she agreed willingly and without hesitation.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'heavily' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The area was heavily affected by the recent flooding.
quests.hint: Degree adverbs come before the participle adjective they modify.
quests.explanation: 'Heavily' before 'affected': 'heavily affected'. It intensifies the degree of impact caused by the flooding.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'solely' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The decision rests solely with the board of directors.
quests.hint: 'Solely' before 'with' limits where responsibility lies.
quests.explanation: 'Solely' before 'with': 'rests solely with the board'. It means no one else shares the responsibility.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'entirely' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The report was entirely based on secondary research.
quests.hint: Degree adverbs come before the word or phrase they modify.
quests.explanation: 'Entirely' before 'based on': 'entirely based on secondary research'. It emphasises the complete reliance on secondary sources.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'greatly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The new policy has greatly benefited local communities.
quests.hint: Degree adverbs come before the verb they intensify.
quests.explanation: 'Greatly' before 'benefited': 'greatly benefited'. It emphasises the significant positive impact of the policy.
